 PUBLIC COMMENT RULES
 “(California Government Code Section 54954.3).
 (a) Every agenda for regular meetings shall provide an opportunity for members of the
 public to directly address the legislative body on any item of interest to the public, before
 or during the legislative body’s consideration of the item, that is within the subject matter
 jurisdiction of the legislative body, provided that no action shall be taken on any item not

 Section 54954.2 [section omitted].

 (b) (1) The legislative body of a local agency may adopt reasonable regulations to ensure
 that the intent of the subdivision (a) is carried out, including, but not limited to, regulations
 limiting the total amount of time allocated for public testimony on particular issues and for
 each individual speaker.

City Council  Wednesday, December 18, 2024
   (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), when the legislative body of a local agency limits
 time for public comment, the legislative body of a local agency shall provide at least twice
 the allotted time to a member of the public who utilizes a translator to ensure that non-
 English speakers receive the same opportunity to directly address the legislative body of
 a local agency.”

 subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council. As specified in the Brown Act, a speaker

SUBJECT:  APPROVE FIRST AMENDMENT TO MEMORANDUM OF
  UNDERSTANDING WITH THE CITY OF PALMDALE TO ACCEPT AN
  INCREASE OF $600,000 OF UNITED STATES TREASURY
  CORONAVIRUS STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL RECOVERY FUNDS
  (SLFRF) UNDER THE AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT (ARPA)
  FUNDS FOR DEVELOPMENT OF AFFORDABLE HOUSING

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the First Amendment to Memorandum of Understanding Agreement No.
  A-8029 with the City of Palmdale to accept an increase of $600,000 of United
  States Treasury Coronavirus SLFRF under the ARPA funds for the development
  of affordable housing; and,

  2. Authorize the Executive Director or her designee to execute the Amendment to
  Memorandum of Understanding Agreement No. A-8029 with the City of
  Palmdale, including minimal and/or non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

The City was awarded $35,445,019 from the U.S. Treasury through the Coronavirus
SLFRF under the ARPA. These funds can be used for various purposes, including
investing in affordable housing to help low-income residents and address the financial
challenges caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. The final rules allow the City to use
these funds to tackle the ongoing housing shortages worsened by the pandemic. Any
program income from repaid loans can be reused for eligible purposes, but there are
restrictions on when the funds can be used.
 Report to Chair and Commissioners of the Housing Authority
Re: Agrmt No. A-8029 First Amendment MOU
December 18, 2024
Page 2

DISCUSSION

The Housing Authority assists developers with gap financing to develop and rehabilitate
affordable units for eligible households with extremely low, very low, and low incomes.
The Housing Authority proposes to loan the ARPA funds granted by the City and program
income received through repayment of the funds from a prior project to develop an eligible
affordable housing project. The Housing Authority plans to use ARPA funds to enter into
a proposed pre-development loan agreement with Linc 4th Street Palmdale, LP. This
agreement will help assess the feasibility of the proposed project, design it, and apply for
the necessary government approvals and financing.

FISCAL IMPACT

$600,000; Funds are available in account 15818503-737100-1332 ARPA Affordable
Housing.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal III: Invest in infrastructure to improve community livability and to plan and maintain
  safe and attractive neighborhoods, streets, and facilities.
  C. Plan and maintain safe and attractive neighborhoods, streets, facilities, and
  public spaces with exciting programming that promotes active fun for everyone.

SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. HA 2024-007, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  HOUSING AUTHORITY OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE APPROVING
  AN EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATION AGREEMENT, A LETTER OF LOAN
  COMMITMENT FOR $9,375,000 AND A PREDEVELOPMENT LOAN
  AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE HOUSING AUTHORITY OF THE CITY
  OF PALMDALE AND LINC 4th STREET PALMDALE, LP FOR
  $1,800,000 FOR PRE-DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES FOR A
  PROPOSED AFFORDABLE HOUSING RENTAL DEVELOPMENT
  LOCATED AT EAST AVENUE Q AND 4th STREET EAST, ON A
  PORTION OF APN 3006-008-921

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Housing Authority of the City of Palmdale:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. HA 2024-007, a Resolution of the Housing Authority of the
  City of Palmdale approving an Exclusive Negotiation Agreement, a Letter of Loan
  Commitment for $9,375,000, and a Predevelopment Loan Agreement between the
  Housing Authority of the City of Palmdale and Linc 4th Street Palmdale, LP for
  $1,800,000 for pre-development activities for a proposed affordable housing rental
  development located at East Avenue Q and 4th Street East, on a portion of APN
  3006-008-921; and,

  2. Authorize the Executive Director or her designee to execute Agreements Nos. A-
  9120 and A-9121 and the Letter of Loan Commitment with Linc 4th Street
  Palmdale, LP, including minimal and/or non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

On May 9, 2005, the former Community Redevelopment Agency of the City of Palmdale
(Redevelopment Agency) approved the acquisition of 10.39 acres of vacant land on the
north side of East Avenue Q between Sumac Avenue and 5th Street East for the
development of affordable housing. The proposed affordable housing would consist of
multi-family rental housing to be owned and operated by a non-profit organization on a
 Report to Chair and Commissioners of the Housing Authority
Re: Reso No. HA 2024-007, Agrmt Nos. A-9120 & A-9121
December 18, 2024
Page 2

portion of the approximately 10-acre site and single-family owner-occupied townhomes
on the remaining portion of the approximately 10-acre site (this remaining portion is
comprised of APNs 3006-008-921 and 3006-008-922 and is referred to herein as the
“Property”).

The State of California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD)
approved an allocation of $9,950,400 of Infill Infrastructure Grant (IIG) funding for the
Transit Village Development. On October 24, 2011, the Redevelopment Agency and the
then Developer, Community Development Associates, entered into IIG Grant Agreement
07-IIG-4212 (IIG Agreement) with HCD, requiring 202 affordable housing units consisting
of 154 multi-family rental units and two (2) manager units (a total of 156 units for the multi-
family portion of the affordable housing) and 46 for-sale townhomes to be built and placed
into operation on the Property. HCD, the Redevelopment Agency, and the then Developer
agreed to assign and have the Housing Authority of the City of Palmdale (Housing
Authority) assume responsibility for the IIG award.

In June 2014, the multi-family rental units, known as Wright Brothers Court, were
completed.

On July 17, 2024, HCD approved an amendment to the IIG Agreement removing the then-
developer, providing for 46 units of for-sale townhomes to be rental housing, and
modifying and extending the IIG’s performance schedule.

DISCUSSION

On May 16, 2024, the Housing Authority released Request for Proposal No. 23-003-6400
(RFP) for Transit Village Affordable Rental Housing Development to develop affordable
rental housing on the two parcels of the Property. The Housing Authority now owns these
parcels, which were acquired through the assumption of housing assets from the former
Redevelopment Agency.

Three responses to the RFP were received. Linc Housing Corporation (Linc) was selected
as a developer through the review and interview process. Linc’s response included the
proposed development of 72 units of affordable housing and a manager unit (Proposed
Project) utilizing approximately 2.2 acres of the Property (Site), a portion of APN 3006-
008-921.

The Housing Authority proposes to commit $1,800,000 in funding from the Department of
the Treasury, Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds under the American
Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) for pre-development activities related to the Proposed Project.
If a Disposition and Development Agreement is entered into, the Housing Authority
proposes to commit Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Funds for the development
of the Proposed Project. The ARPA Funds would be loaned to Linc 4th Street Palmdale,
pursuant to the proposed Predevelopment Loan Agreement. The Predevelopment Loan
 Report to Chair and Commissioners of the Housing Authority
Re: Reso No. HA 2024-007, Agrmt Nos. A-9120 & A-9121
December 18, 2024
Page 3

Agreement provides for Linc to assess the Proposed Project’s feasibility, design the
Proposed Project, and apply for governmental approvals and construction financing.

In addition, the Housing Authority proposes to enter into an Exclusive Negotiation
Agreement and Letter of Loan Commitment for $9,375,000 to negotiate the terms and
conditions of a Disposition and Development Agreement to be submitted for consideration
by the Housing Authority Board.

The Predevelopment Loan Agreement, Exclusive Negotiation Agreement, and Letter of
Loan Commitment are the early-stage agreements often entered into before a lead
agency decides on the specifics of a project. Until Linc has submitted a formal application
for entitlements and received City of Palmdale (City) approval for such entitlements and
associated environmental review as required by the California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA), which approvals may be granted or denied in the City’s sole discretion, neither
the City nor the Housing Authority will have committed to approving the Proposed Project
or disposing of the Site. The specific parameters of the Proposed Project are unknown at
this stage. Therefore, it is premature to conduct a meaningful analysis and environmental
review of the Proposed Project under CEQA. Once Linc submits the Proposed Project to
the City with a formal application, the CEQA environmental review will be performed. A
Disposition and Development Agreement would not be submitted to the Housing Authority
Board until such CEQA environmental review has been performed.

FISCAL IMPACT

$11,175,000; Funds are available in the amount of $1,800,000 under the American
Rescue Plan Act and $9,375,000 in Housing Asset Funds.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal III: Invest in infrastructure to improve community livability

  C. Plan and maintain safe and attractive neighborhoods, streets, facilities, and public
  spaces with exciting programming that promotes active fun for everyone.

  E. Transform housing inventory to meet the changing lifestyle and market
  demands.

  WHEREAS, The City Council of the City of Palmdale (“City Council”)
adopted the Redevelopment Plans for the Merged Redevelopment Projects (“Project
Area”) on March 24, 1994, by Ordinances Nos. 1042, 1043, and 1044, which resulted in
the allocation of property taxes from the Project Area to the former Community
Redevelopment Agency of the City of Palmdale (“Redevelopment Agency”) for purposes
of redevelopment. On May 4, 2011, the City Council adopted the Expansion Area
Amendment by Ordinance No. 1418, adding additional territory to the Merged Project
Area and amending and restating the redevelopment plans into a single Amended and
Restated Redevelopment Plan for the Merged Project Area. Project Area No. 2, Project
Area No. 3, Project Area No. 4, and the Expansion Area collectively are referred to as
the “Merged Project Area”. On May 4, 2011, the City Council adopted the Expansion
Area Amendment by Ordinance No. 1418, adding additional territory to the Merged
Project Area and amending and restating the redevelopment plans into a single
Amended and Restated Redevelopment Plan for the Merged Project Area
(“Redevelopment Plan”). Project Area No. 2, Project Area No. 3, Project Area No. 4, and
the Expansion Area collectively are referred to as the “Merged Project Area”; and

  WHEREAS, The Housing Authority of the City of Palmdale (“Authority”) is
implementing certain proposed uses in the Merged Project Area, including low-income
housing, which use will aid in carrying out the Redevelopment Plan, pursuant to its
obligations under Assembly Bill No. 26 (2011-2012 1st Ex. Sess.), as amended by
Assembly Bill No. 1484 (2011-2012 Regular Session), and as further amended from
time to time (collectively, the “Dissolution Bills”) wherein the Authority, as the designated
entity, will perform the housing functions previously performed by the former
Redevelopment Agency, including to carry out the purposes of the Dissolution Bills; and

  WHEREAS, In accordance with its obligations under the Dissolution Bills, the
Authority wishes to enter into a proposed Exclusive Negotiation Agreement and Letter
of Loan Commitment with Linc 4th Street Palmdale, LP. The two entities propose to
negotiate the terms for developing the proposed affordable rental housing to be located

at the northeast corner of East Avenue Q and 4th Street East (“Site”) and the terms and

  ARPA ACT REQUIREMENTS

RECITAL:
  On March 11, 2021, the American Rescue Plan Act (“ARP Act”) was signed into
law. The ARP Act was intended to provide increased aid to individuals, families,
businesses, and governments affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. The ARP Act
established and funded the Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (the
“CSLFRF”), which included two hundred forty (240) billion dollars for state, territorial,
local, and Tribal governments that are being used to fight the pandemic and accelerate
local economic recovery.

MANDATORY CONTRACT PROVISIONS FOR ARP ACT EXPENDITURES:

Procurement processes for expenditures using American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA)
funds generally follow state and local rules. In most cases, city procurement policies will
satisfy the federal requirements. One notable difference is that federal procurement
regulations mandate specific contract provisions in certain circumstances. There are no
requirements for contracts or expenditures of less than $10,000. However, using ARPA
funds for contracts in excess of $10,000 triggers the mandatory contract provisions in 2
CFR Part 200, Appendix II.
 Most contract provisions are required only on those exceeding $100,000 or those for
construction projects of any amount. However, mandatory contract provisions will apply
if a city obligates ARPA funds to a contract that exceeds $100,000.

For ease of administration, below is an explanation of the mandatory contract provisions
and model language necessary for compliance with federal law disclosures.

2 C.F.R. PART 200: APPENDIX II, CONTRACT PROVISIONS

  •  For contracts over $10,000, cities must include a provision that addresses
  termination for cause and convenience by the local government, including the
  process for termination and the basis for settlement.
  •  For contracts over $100,000, cities must include a provision that addresses
  administrative, contractual, or legal remedies if a contractor violates or breaches
  the contract, including sanctions and penalties for the breach.
  •  In accepting the ARPA award, local governments agreed to include an EEO
  statement in any federally assisted construction contract defined in 41 CFR Part
  60-1.3. A federally assisted construction contract is defined as follows:
  o Any agreement or modification thereof between any applicant and a
  person for construction work which is paid for in whole or in part with funds
  obtained from the government or borrowed on the credit of the
  government pursuant to any federal program involving a grant, contract,
  loan, insurance, or guarantee, or undertaken pursuant to any federal
  program involving such grant, contract, loan, insurance, or guarantee, or
  any application or modification thereof approved by the government for a
  grant, contract, loan, insurance, or guarantee under which the applicant
  itself participates in the construction work.

2.  Description of Site.

which is generally located on the northeast corner of Avenue Q and 4th Street East in Palmdale,
California, which is a portion of APN 3006-008-921, and is illustrated by the Site Map in Exhibit
A, which is attached to this Agreement and hereby incorporated by reference (the “Site”).

3.  Grant of Right of Entry.

  (a) Subject to and conditioned upon the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the
Authority grants to Linc and its authorized agents a non-exclusive right of entry (the “Right of
Entry”) to perform the following acts on the Site: (1) conduct any reasonable, due diligence with
respect to the Property, including but not limited to: (x) reviewing plans, specifications, permits,
approvals, reports, leases, contracts, files and records relating to the ownership, construction,
development, financing, permitting and marketing of the Property; and (y) performing invasive
testing, surveys and inspections with respect to the environmental and physical condition of the
Property, (2) (obtain soil samples and make surveys and tests necessary to determine the suitability
of the Site for the development of the Proposed Project; and (3) conduct reasonable investigations
on and beneath the Site and all improvements thereon to determine the presence of Hazardous
Materials. As used herein, the phrase “Hazardous Materials” means any substance, whether in
the form of a solid, liquid, gas or any other form whatsoever, which by any governmental
requirements is defined as “hazardous” or harmful to the environment.

without obtaining the Authority’s prior written consent.

“Term”).

ordinances, regulations, rules, and orders with respect to the Site. Linc and Linc’s Representatives

material, waste or substance unless such items are used in the ordinary course of Linc’s and Linc’s
Representatives’ permitted activities under the Right of Entry. The term “hazardous” shall include
any substance, material, waste pollutant, contaminant, or matter now or hereafter regulated by any
environmental law, rule or regulation. Linc and Linc’s Representatives shall conduct all of its
operations on the Site in connection with this Agreement at Linc’s sole cost and expense.

TERMS AND CONDITIONS

1.  The Proposed Project will consist of Borrower’s ground lease of the Site and the new
  construction of approximately 73 units of rental housing. At least thirty percent (30%) of
  the affordable units must be occupied by and restricted to extremely low income
  households (30% AMI) at rents that do not exceed the applicable affordable rent specified
  in Health & Safety Code section 50053 for extremely low income households. The
  remaining units (with the exception of one management unit) must be occupied by and
  restricted to lower income households pursuant to the California Tax Credit Allocation
  Committee (60% of Los Angeles County area median income or lower), at affordable rents
  provided that rents for these units shall not exceed the affordable rent for a household at
  59% AMI under Health & Safety Code section 50053. All units shall be restricted for a
  minimum of fifty-five (55) years, but no less than the term of the ground lease.

2.  This loan commitment is contingent upon the Housing Authority receiving evidence
  reasonably acceptable to it that Borrower has or will obtain adequate and appropriate
  financing for the Project, which may include a reservation of Low Income Housing Tax
  Credits from the California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (“CTCAC”).

3.  The Housing Authority Loan will be an amount equal to the aggregate of (a) the lesser of
  (I) appraised value of the land and (II) $2,000,000; and (b) a development loan in the
  original principal amount of $7,375,000, each with a term of 55 years or such longer period
  as mutually agreed upon and simple interest at 3% per annum (or such higher rate on the
  land portion of the loan if requested by Linc) from the date of disbursal. Payments on the
  Housing Authority Loan shall be payable exclusively from the Housing Authority’s pro
  rata share (as a percentage of public financing as mutually agreed to by the Housing
  Authority and Linc) of 50% (subject to adjustment proposed by Borrower and approved by
  the Housing Authority) of annual residual receipts, net sale proceeds and net refinancing
  proceeds, or upon such other repayment terms mutually agreed to by the Housing Authority
  and Linc. The terms of the Residual Receipts obligation, including identification of all of
  Borrower’s obligations having a priority over the Housing Authority’s right to receive
  Residual Receipts, will be set forth in the promissory note(s) to be attached to the
  hereinafter defined DDA.

4.  This commitment is based on Borrower’s current estimates of total development costs,
  including demolition costs. Borrower will be responsible, without cost to the Housing
  Authority, for any additional sources of funds that may be needed to complete the Proposed
  Project. Borrower agrees that the Housing Authority Loan will be reduced to the extent the

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-091, a Resolution of the City Council of the City
  of Palmdale authorizing the City Manager to execute agreements with the
  California Department of Tax and Fee Administration for implementation of a local
  transactions and use tax; and,

  2. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-095, a Resolution of the City Council of the City
  of Palmdale authorizing the examination of sales or transactions and use tax
  records; and,

  3. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute all agreements and
  associated documents, including minimal and/or non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND

On July 10, 2024, the City Council approved Resolution No. CC 2024-070 placing a
local Transactions and Use Tax measure (“Measure PD”) on the November 5, 2024
ballot for voter consideration.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Measure PD
December 18, 2024
Page 2

On November 5, 2024, the City of Palmdale voters passed Measure PD with 54.99% of
the total votes in favor of the Measure. Staff is requesting the CDTFA to administer the
collection and distribution of this tax and allow the City of Palmdale and third-party
consultant, Hinderliter, de Llamas & Associates (HdL), to examine the sales, use, and
transaction tax records. Collection of this new revenue will commence on April 1, 2025.

DISCUSSION

The CDTFA is already providing administration services for the collection, distribution,
and reporting of the 1% Bradley Burns tax and the 0.75% Measure AV tax. The CDTFA
is requesting a new agreement for the one-time preparation and ongoing administration
of the 0.75%, or ¾ of a cent, Measure PD sales, transactions and use tax. In addition to
the agreements, the CDTFA is requesting a list of City Staff authorized to examine the
sales, transactions and use tax records, and requests to name a third-party consultant
firm, if applicable.

FISCAL IMPACT

$175,000; The CDTFA Preparatory Fees are a one-time cost to the City and is not to
exceed $175,000. Administration Fees for CDTFA services are ongoing, and such
amounts shall be deducted from the taxes collected by the CDTFA for the City.

STRATEGIC PLAN

Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.

  transparency.

  AGREEMENT FOR PREPARATION TO ADMINISTER AND OPERATE
  CITY'S TRANSACTIONS AND USE TAX ORDINANCE

  In order to prepare to administer a transactions and use tax ordinance adopted in accordance with
the provision of Part 1.6 (commencing with Section 7251) of Division 2 of the Revenue and Taxation
Code, the City of Palmdale, hereinafter called City, and the CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF TAX
AND FEE ADMINISTRATION, hereinafter called Department, do agree as follows:

  1. The Department agrees to enter into work to prepare to administer and operate a transactions
and use tax in conformity with Part 1.6 of Division 2 of the Revenue and Taxation Code which has been
approved by a majority of the electors of the City and whose ordinance has been adopted by the City.

  2. City agrees to pay to the Department at the times and in the amounts hereinafter specified all
of the Department's costs for preparatory work necessary to administer the City's transactions and use
tax ordinance. The Department's costs for preparatory work include costs of developing procedures,
programming for data processing, developing and adopting appropriate regulations, designing and
printing forms, developing instructions for the Department's staff and for taxpayers, and other
appropriate and necessary preparatory costs to administer a transactions and use tax ordinance. These
costs shall include both direct and indirect costs as specified in Section 11256 of the Government Code.

  3. Preparatory costs may be accounted for in a manner which conforms to the internal
accounting and personnel records currently maintained by the Department. The billings for costs may be
presented in summary form. Detailed records of preparatory costs will be retained for audit and
verification by the City.

  4. Any dispute as to the amount of preparatory costs incurred by the Department shall be
referred to the State Director of Finance for resolution, and the Director's decision shall be final.

  5. Preparatory costs incurred by the Department shall be billed by the Department periodically,
with the final billing within a reasonable time after the operative date of the ordinance. City shall pay
to the Department the amount of such costs on or before the last day of the next succeeding month
following the month when the billing is received.

  6. The amount to be paid by City for the Department's preparatory costs shall not exceed one
hundred seventy-five thousand dollars ($175,000) (Revenue and Taxation Code Section 7272.)

  AGREEMENT FOR STATE ADMINISTRATION
  OF CITY TRANSACTIONS AND USE TAXES

  The City Council of the City of Palmdale has adopted, and the voters of the City of
Palmdale (hereafter called “City” or “District”) have approved by the required majority vote, the City of
Palmdale Transactions and Use Tax Ordinance (hereafter called “Ordinance”), a copy of which is
attached hereto. To carry out the provisions of Part 1.6 of Division 2 of the Revenue and Taxation Code
and the Ordinance, the California State Department of Tax and Fee Administration, (hereinafter called
the “Department”) and the City do agree as follows:

  ARTICLE I
  DEFINITIONS

  Unless the context requires otherwise, wherever the following terms appear in the Agreement,
they shall be interpreted to mean the following:

  1. "District taxes" shall mean the transactions and use taxes, penalties, and interest imposed
under an ordinance specifically authorized by Revenue and Taxation code Section 7265, and in
compliance with Part 1.6, Division 2 of the Revenue and Taxation Code.

  2. "City Ordinance" shall mean the City's Transactions and Use Tax Ordinance referred to above
and attached hereto, Ordinance No. 1644, as amended from time to time, or as deemed to be amended
from time to time pursuant to Revenue and Taxation Code Section 7262.2.

  ARTICLE II
  ADMINISTRATION AND COLLECTION
  OF CITY TAXES

  A. Administration.  The Department and City agree that the Department shall perform
exclusively all functions incident to the administration and operation of the City Ordinance.
   B. Other Applicable Laws. City agrees that all provisions of law applicable to the
administration and operation of the Department Sales and Use Tax Law which are not inconsistent with
Part 1.6 of Division 2 of the Revenue and Taxation Code shall be applicable to the administration and
operation of the City Ordinance. City agrees that money collected pursuant to the City Ordinance may
be deposited into the State Treasury to the credit of the Retail Sales Tax Fund and may be drawn from
that Fund for any authorized purpose, including making refunds, compensating and reimbursing the
Department pursuant to Article IV of this Agreement, and transmitting to City the amount to which City
is entitled.

  C. Transmittal of money.

  1. For the period during which the tax is in effect, and except as otherwise provided herein, all
district taxes collected under the provisions of the City Ordinance shall be transmitted to City
periodically as promptly as feasible, but not less often than twice in each calendar quarter.

  2. For periods subsequent to the expiration date of the tax whether by City’s self-imposed limits
or by final judgment of any court of the State of California holding that City’s ordinance is invalid or
void, all district taxes collected under the provisions of the City Ordinance shall be transmitted to City
not less than once in each calendar quarter.

  3. Transmittals may be made by mail or electronic funds transfer to an account of the City
designated and authorized by the City. A statement shall be furnished at least quarterly indicating the
amounts withheld pursuant to Article IV of this Agreement.

  D. Rules. The Department shall prescribe and adopt such rules and regulations as in its
judgment are necessary or desirable for the administration and operation of the City Ordinance and the
distribution of the district taxes collected thereunder.

  E. Preference. Unless the payor instructs otherwise, and except as otherwise provided in this
Agreement, the Department shall give no preference in applying money received for state sales and use
taxes, state-administered local sales and use taxes, and district transactions and use taxes owed by a
taxpayer, but shall apply moneys collected to the satisfaction of the claims of the State, cities, counties,
cities and counties, redevelopment agencies, other districts, and City as their interests appear.

(Rev. 7/24)  2
   F. Security. The Department agrees that any security which it hereafter requires to be furnished
by taxpayers under the State Sales and Use Tax Law will be upon such terms that it also will be available
for the payment of the claims of City for district taxes owing to it as its interest appears. The Department
shall not be required to change the terms of any security now held by it, and City shall not participate in
any security now held by the Department.

  G. Records of the Department.

  When requested by resolution of the legislative body of the City under section 7056 of the
Revenue and Taxation Code, the Department agrees to permit authorized personnel of the City to
examine the records of the Department, including the name, address, and account number of each seller
holding a seller’s permit with a registered business location in the City, pertaining to the ascertainment
of transactions and use taxes collected for the City. Information obtained by the City from examination
of the Department's records shall be used by the City only for purposes related to the collection of
transactions and use taxes by the Department pursuant to this Agreement.

  H. Annexation. City agrees that the Department shall not be required to give effect to an
annexation, for the purpose of collecting, allocating, and distributing District transactions and use taxes,
earlier than the first day of the calendar quarter which commences not less than two months after notice
to the Department. The notice shall include the name of the county or counties annexed to the extended
City boundary. In the event the City shall annex an area, the boundaries of which are not coterminous
with a county or counties, the notice shall include a description of the area annexed and two maps of the
City showing the area annexed and the location address of the property nearest to the extended City
boundary on each side of every street or road crossing the boundary.

  ARTICLE III
  ALLOCATION OF TAX

  A. Allocation. In the administration of the Department's contracts with all districts that impose
transactions and use taxes imposed under ordinances, which comply with Part 1.6 of Division 2 of the
Revenue and Taxation Code:

  1. Any payment not identified as being in payment of liability owing to a designated district
or districts may be apportioned among the districts as their interest appear, or, in the discretion of the
(Rev. 7/24)  3
 Department, to all districts with which the Department has contracted using ratios reflected by the
distribution of district taxes collected from all taxpayers.

  2. All district taxes collected as a result of determinations or billings made by the
Department, and all amounts refunded or credited may be distributed or charged to the respective districts
in the same ratio as the taxpayer's self-declared district taxes for the period for which the determination,
billing, refund or credit applies.

  B. Vehicles, Vessels, and Aircraft. For the purpose of allocating use tax with respect to
vehicles, vessels, or aircraft, the address of the registered owner appearing on the application for
registration or on the certificate of ownership may be used by the Department in determining the place
of use.

  ARTICLE IV
  COMPENSATION

  The City agrees to pay to the Department as the State's cost of administering the City Ordinance

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Successor Agency to the Community Redevelopment
Agency of the City of Palmdale:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. SA 2024-014 approving the Recognized Obligation
  Payment Schedule (ROPS 25-26) for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30,
  2026.

  2. Adopt Resolution No. SA 2024-015 approving the Administrative Budget for the
  Period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 (Administrative Budget 2025-26).

BACKGROUND

Assembly Bill 1X 26 (AB 26) was signed by the Governor on June 28, 2011, and upheld
as constitutional by the California Supreme Court. On June 27, 2012, the Governor
signed Assembly Bill 1484 (AB 1484). AB 26 and AB 1484 (together the Dissolution
Bills) made sweeping changes to California Redevelopment Law, eliminating
redevelopment agencies statewide, establishing successor agencies, and requiring the
successor agencies to pay, perform, and enforce the enforceable obligations of the
former redevelopment agencies and to wind down the affairs of the former
redevelopment agencies.
 Report to Chair and Directors of the Successor Agency
Re: Adopt Resolution Nos. SA 2024-014 and SA 2024-015
December 18, 2024
Page 2

Administrative Budget

Section 34177(j) of the Dissolution Bills requires the Successor Agency to prepare an
Administrative Budget annually and submit it to the Los Angeles County Fifth
Supervisorial District Consolidated Oversight Board for approval.

Section 34177(k) of the Dissolution Bills further requires the Successor Agency to
provide the Los Angeles County Auditor-Controller the administrative cost estimates
from its approved Administrative Budget to be paid from property tax revenues
deposited in the Redevelopment Property Tax Trust Fund.

Health & Safety Code Section 34171(b)(3) states that commencing July 1, 2016, the
administrative cost allowance shall be up to 3 percent of the actual property tax
distributed to the successor agency by the county auditor-controller in the preceding
fiscal year for payment of approved enforceable obligations, reduced by the successor
agency’s administrative cost allowance and loan repayments made to the city pursuant
to Section 34191.4(b) during the preceding fiscal year, subject to a minimum of
$250,000, unless such amount is reduced by the Oversight Board or by agreement
between the successor agency and the State Department of Finance (“Department of
Finance”). Staff has estimated this amount and allocated it to various Successor Agency
costs as detailed in Exhibit A to Resolution No. SA 2024-014.

Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule (ROPS)

Section 34177(l) of the Dissolution Bills requires the Successor Agency to prepare a
Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule (ROPS) listing the enforceable obligations of
the former Redevelopment Agency annually.

Section 34177(l) further requires that (i) the ROPS shall be submitted to the county
administrative officer, the Los Angeles County Auditor-Controller (Auditor-Controller)
and the State Department of Finance (Department of Finance) at the same time that the
Successor Agency submits the ROPS to the Los Angeles County Fifth Supervisorial
District Consolidated Oversight Board for approval; (ii) the ROPS shall be submitted to
and duly approved by the Los Angeles County Fifth Supervisorial District Consolidated
Oversight Board; (iii) the approved ROPS shall be posted on the Successor Agency’s
website; and (iv) the approved ROPS shall be submitted to the Auditor-Controller, the
State Controller and the State Department of Finance.

Section 34180 of the Dissolution Bills (Section 34180) requires certain successor
agency actions to be approved by the oversight board, including Section 34180(c)
“Setting aside of amounts in reserves as required by indentures, trust indentures, or
similar documents governing the issuance of outstanding redevelopment agency
bonds.” The attached ROPS 25-26 details amounts in accordance with Section
34180(c).
 Report to Chair and Directors of the Successor Agency
Re: Adopt Resolution Nos. SA 2024-014 and SA 2024-015
December 18, 2024
Page 3

The attached ROPS 25-26 also includes an enforceable obligation for the repayment of
the Educational Revenue Augmentation Fund (ERAF) and Supplemental Educational
Revenue Augmentation Fund (SERAF) loans borrowed from the former Redevelopment
Agency’s Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund.

Senate Bill No. 107 (section 14 of Chapter 325, Statutes of 2015) states that the
Successor Agency’s Oversight Board continues to exist and will only cease to exist after
all of its indebtedness has been repaid, and thus, requires that the City’s Successor
Agency’s Oversight Board approve ROPS 25-26.

DISCUSSION

The attached Resolution Nos. SA 2024-014 and SA 2024-015 seek approval of the
Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule (ROPS) 25-26 and the Administrative Budget
25-26.

Approval of the ROPS and the Administrative Budget will allow the City to remain in
compliance with AB 26 and AB 1484 (together the Dissolution Bills), and to submit the
information timely to the county administrative officer, the Los Angeles County Auditor-
Controller (Auditor-Controller) and the State Department of Finance (Department of
Finance). Simultaneously, the Successor Agency submits the ROPS to the Los Angeles
County Fifth Supervisorial District Consolidated Oversight Board for approval.

Upon approval from the Los Angeles County Fifth Supervisorial District Consolidated
Oversight Board, and the State Department of Finance, the City may then incorporate the
requested administrative budgets and payments from the ROPS into its annual budget
for Fiscal Year 2025-26.

FISCAL IMPACT

The Administrative Budget for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 totals
$321,605. These funds will be included in various line items in Program 20 of Fund
460 in the fiscal year 2025-26 budget and are included on the ROPS. These funds will
be used to reimburse the City for its staff hours.

The total payments estimated during the one-year period of ROPS 25-26 is $17,110,708,
of which $11,523,210 is expected to be funded by Redevelopment Property Tax Trust
Funds (RPTTF) to be received from the Los Angeles County Auditor-Controller (including
Administrative Cost Allowance), $5,499,275 is from reserve balance funds received in the
prior year, and $88,223 is from other funds. Amounts are to be budgeted in various areas
of the Successor Agency and Housing Successor Agency budgets.

  RESOLUTION NO. SA 2024-015

  A RESOLUTION OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE COMMUNITY
  REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE APPROVING
  THE ADMINISTRATIVE BUDGET FOR THE PERIOD OF JULY 1, 2025
  THROUGH JUNE 30, 2026 (ADMINISTRATIVE BUDGET 25-26).

  WHEREAS, The Community Redevelopment Agency of the City of Palmdale
(“Redevelopment Agency”) was a redevelopment agency in the City of Palmdale (“City”),
duly created pursuant to the California Community Redevelopment Law (Part 1
(commencing with SECTION 33000) of Division 24 of the California Health and Safety
Code) (“Redevelopment Law”); and

  WHEREAS, The Redevelopment Agency was responsible for the administration
of redevelopment activities within the City; and

  WHEREAS, Assembly Bill 1X 26 (“AB 26”) was signed by the Governor on June
28, 2011 and upheld to be constitutional by the California Supreme Court on December
29, 2011; and

  WHEREAS, AB 26 made certain changes to the California Community
Redevelopment Law (Part 1 (commencing with Section 33000) of Division 24 of the
California Health and Safety Code), including adding Part 1.8 (commencing with Section
34161) and Part 1.85 (commencing with Section 34170) (“Part 1.85”) to Division 24 of
the California Health and Safety Code (“Health and Safety Code”); and

  WHEREAS, On February 1, 2012, as a result of the Supreme Court’s decision,
all California redevelopment agencies were dissolved, successor agencies were
established as successor agencies to the former redevelopment agencies pursuant to
Health and Safety Code Section 34173, and successor agencies are tasked with paying,
performing and enforcing the enforceable obligations of the former redevelopment
agencies and winding down the affairs of the former redevelopment agencies; and

  WHEREAS, On June 27, 2012, the Governor of California signed Assembly Bill
1484 (“AB 1484”) into law, making several substantive and technical amendments to AB
26 (AB 26 and AB 1484 together referred to as the “Dissolution Bills”); and

  WHEREAS, On January 4, 2012, the City Council adopted Resolution No. CC
2012-002 declaring itself as the Successor Agency to the Community Redevelopment
Agency of the City of Palmdale (“Successor Agency”) upon the dissolution of the
Redevelopment Agency; and

  WHEREAS, On April 4, 2012 the City Council, acting in its capacity as the
Successor Agency, adopted Resolution No. CC 2012-041 SA naming itself the
“Successor Agency to the Community Redevelopment Agency of the City of Palmdale”,
the sole name by which it will exercise its powers and fulfill its duties pursuant to Part
1.85 of AB 26, and establishing itself as a separate legal entity with rules and regulations
that will apply to the governance and operations of the Successor Agency; and

  WHEREAS, pursuant to Health and Safety Code Section 34179 (q), commencing
on and after July 1, 2018, the County of Los Angeles, where more than 40 oversight
boards were created by the Dissolution Act, shall have five consolidated oversight
boards, each encompassing the five supervisorial districts; and

  WHEREAS, the Fifth Supervisorial District Consolidated Oversight Board ("Fifth
District Consolidated Oversight Board") has jurisdiction over the Successor Agency of
the Former Redevelopment Agency to the City of Palmdale and

  WHEREAS, the Fifth District Consolidated Oversight Board will hold a
regular/special meeting on or about January 9, 2025; and

  WHEREAS, Health and Safety Code Section 34177(j) (“Section 34177(j)”)
requires the Successor Agency to prepare an administrative budget for the period July
1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 and submit the administrative budget to the Los Angeles
County Fifth Supervisorial District Consolidated Oversight Board for approval. The
administrative budget shall include all of the following: (i) estimated amounts for
Successor Agency administrative costs for the upcoming annual fiscal period; (ii)
proposed sources of payment for Successor Agency administrative costs; and (iii)
proposals for arrangements for administrative and operations services provided by the
City or other entity; and

  WHEREAS, Health and Safety Code Section 34177(k) (“Section 34177(k)”)
requires the Successor Agency to provide to the Los Angeles County Auditor-Controller
for the period July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026 the administrative cost estimates from
its approved administrative budget that are to be paid from property tax revenues (i.e.
former tax increment revenues) deposited in the County’s Redevelopment Property Tax
Trust Fund established for the Successor Agency; and

  WHEREAS, Health & Safety Code SECTION 34179.7 (o) (1), requires the
Successor Agency to prepare a forward-looking, annual Recognized Obligation
Payment Schedule (ROPS) listing the enforceable obligations of the former
Redevelopment Agency that are due in the next annual period and submitting an
oversight board approved annual ROPS to the Department of Finance and Auditor-
Controller by February 1, 2025; and

  WHEREAS, Health & Safety Code Section 34171(b)(3) states that, the
administrative cost allowance shall be up to 3 percent of the actual property tax

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8955 with New Creation Builders, Inc. for design and
  build services for PN 902, Emergency Operations Center (EOC) Tenant
  Improvement Project for a not to exceed amount of $5,113,831; includes a 10%
  contingency of $397,736 and compliance labor cost of $22,815 for a term of 350
  working days from the date of the Notice to Proceed; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8955
  with New Creation Builders, Inc. including minimal and/or non-substantial
  changes.

BACKGROUND

The City has identified a space in the Aero Building located at 38255 9th Street East to
use as the EOC to provide emergency operations and support during declared local,
state, and national emergencies. The identified space is currently vacant and includes the
desired space to house EOC equipment and staff.

As the City's population grows and the complexity of potential incidents increases, the
current EOC lacks the physical infrastructure to support a full-scale, coordinated
response. It is also limited in size, which hinders its capacity to house the critical
personnel, equipment, and technology essential for managing large-scale emergencies.
 Report to Mayor and City Council

The proposed EOC will be equipped to accommodate up to 36 operational workstations,
ensuring the City is fully prepared to respond to any incident that may threaten public
health and safety, infrastructure, or essential services. Additionally, the center’s layout
will be designed to enhance communication flow, enabling various departments to
coordinate efforts seamlessly during high-stakes incidents. Response personnel will be
able to work in a cohesive environment that enables swift information sharing and
decision-making, allowing rapid assessment and addressing of evolving situations in real
time.

The design and construction of an EOC will improve the effectiveness of emergency
services as Palmdale grows. It will also provide a plan to coordinate emergencies with
hospitals, schools, major businesses, utilities, the Red Cross, churches, and other service
providers to work together and train in preparation for a coordinated response during a
major event.

DISCUSSION

On July 25, 2024, a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) was released on PlanetBids to
procure a design/build team to design and build the required improvements to the
proposed location. Seventy-two prospective bidders downloaded the bid documents. On
August 27, 2024, one proposal was received, and the City reviewed, vetted, and
interviewed the design/build team. The price proposal incorporated most of the basic
needs for the emergency operations center included in the RFQ.

Staff recommends the award of a design-build agreement to New Creation Builders, Inc.

funds will be used for construction for $3,801,331.

Palmdale, a public entity ("City"), and NEW CREATION BUILDERS, INC., a
Corporation ("Contractor"). Contractor and City are collectively referred to herein as
the “parties.” This Contract shall become effective on the date of the last signatory.

1  Scope of Work

Contractor shall complete the Project in accordance with this Contract. Contractor
shall furnish all materials and perform all work required for the completion of the
following Project:

The Project will be located at 38255 9th Street East, Palmdale, CA 93550.

The project scope includes the design, engineering, permitting and renovations of a
section of the existing courthouse building to transform it into a fully functional EOC
including modifications necessary to the existing building for seismic and ADA
compliance.

The EOC will consist of a single-story structure of approximately 10,000 square
feet, with separate locker rooms with showers, training/meeting room,
operations/media room, break room with kitchen, central emergency operations
room, IT server room, and ADA compliant walkways, doorways, and ramps.

Other appurtenances include but are not limited to an emergency power generator
capable of carrying full load of all site/station circuits, parking lot striping, all
furniture, fixtures, equipment, HVAC, roofing, if needed, landscape and hardscape.
The Project design and materials will be functional as well as compatible with the
character of the City’s vision.

The project to be proposed in the RFP will include all design, engineering, permits,
grading, construction, material, labor, special observation, inspection, testing,
verification, procurement and installation of all equipment. D-B-E will be responsible
for obtaining all required permits, including federal, state, and local governance as
well as coordination with all utilities and other regulatory agencies, start-up and
commissioning required for occupancy and operations. The final proposal must be
the total cost for delivery of the entire project and all of its related elements, and no
further payment will be allowed, therefore.

Procurement processes for expenditures using American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA)
funds generally follow state and local rules. In most cases, city procurement policies
will satisfy the federal requirements. One notable difference is that federal
procurement regulations mandate specific contract provisions in certain
circumstances. There are no requirements for contracts or expenditures of less than
$10,000. However, using ARPA funds for contracts in excess of $10,000 triggers the
mandatory contract provisions in 2 CFR Part 200, Appendix II.

Most contract provisions are required only on those exceeding $100,000 or those for
construction projects of any amount. However, mandatory contract provisions will
apply if a city obligates ARPA funds to a contract that exceeds $100,000.

For ease of administration, below is an explanation of the mandatory contract
provisions and model language necessary for compliance with federal law
disclosures.

2 C.F.R. PART 200: APPENDIX II, CONTRACT PROVISIONS

  • For contracts over $10,000, cities must include a provision that addresses
  termination for cause and convenience by the local government, including the
  process for termination and the basis for settlement.
  • For contracts over $100,000, cities must include a provision that addresses
  administrative, contractual, or legal remedies if a contractor violates or
  breaches the contract, including sanctions and penalties for the breach.
  • In accepting the ARPA award, local governments agreed to include an EEO
  statement in any federally assisted construction contract defined in 41 CFR
  Part 60-1.3. A federally assisted construction contract is defined as follows:
  o Any agreement or modification thereof between any applicant and a

  government pursuant to any federal program involving a grant, contract,

BACKGROUND

For over 40 years, South Antelope Valley Emergency Services (SAVES) has supported
the working poor, disadvantaged, emancipated youth, the homeless, and senior citizens
in the South Antelope Valley by providing food, short-term shelter, clothing, transportation
passes, and programs such as holiday meal preparation, gift baskets, and back-to-school
assistance. SAVES serves about 6,000 clients each year, steadily increasing, having
tripled in the past decade. To keep up with the growing demand, expansion is essential.

Additionally, SAVES receives more donated food and items, requiring extra storage
space, and currently uses off-site storage to manage this need. To better serve the
community, SAVES needs more space for various services, including:

    Storing over 900,000 pounds of donations each year;
    Expanding donation services such as clothing, household items, and toys;
    Offering healthy living classes;
    Connecting clients with local resource providers and advisors;
    Organizing annual food and toy drives.

Larger facilities will also improve SAVES' ability to respond to emergencies like natural
disasters, pandemics, or economic downturns, enhancing preparedness and resilience.

SAVES' daily operations and staffing are funded through the City’s Community
Development Block Grant (CDBG), public service funds, Emergency Food and Shelter
grants, and Measure AV funding. Food is provided through a partnership with the Los
Angeles Regional Food Bank and federal programs.

On August 3, 2022, the City Council approved the acquisition of real property located at
38820 3rd Street East (APN 3006-008-925) and two adjacent parcels (APN 3006-008-
923 and APN 3006-008-924). The acquired building is an 8,250-square-foot
prefabricated metal warehouse that will house a portion of the SAVES facility.

On September 19, 2023, John A. Martin & Associates, Inc. completed an evaluation of
the existing prefabricated metal building, also known as a “Butler Building”, for structural
and seismic integrity. The report’s conclusion identified a series of structural deficiencies
and provided a list of recommended actions for structural strengthening.

DISCUSSION

On August 26, 2024, the City released a design-build Request For Proposals (RFP) to
solicit services from architects and builders to relocate the existing SAVES operations
to the new site and to design the necessary tenant improvements.

The RFP was advertised for eight weeks, with a bid closing date of October 23, 2024.
Two bids were received and only one was deemed responsive. The RFP stipulated that
the project has a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) for each phase of the project.
Phase 1 (Design) GMP is $700,000, and Phase 2 (Construction) GMP is $7,000,000,
for a total project GMP of $7,700,000.

  of City-owned land (APN 3128-015-903), for right-of-way and bikeway
  requirements along 10th Street West and Columbia Way (Avenue M) for public
  road and highway purposes.

BACKGROUND

On March 7, 2023, the City processed a lot line adjustment to reconfigure City-owned
parcels with the Antelope Valley Business Park Specific Plan, thus creating an 8.40-
acre corner parcel at the southeast corner of 10th Street West and Columbia Way
(Avenue M). The City owns this undeveloped parcel in fee and is identified as Assessor
Parcel No. 3128-015-903. As part of entitlement for the Palmdale DC Industrial project,
under Minor Modification No. 22-057 and Site Plan Review 21-005, the developer is
conditioned to provide street improvements along the frontages of this City-owned
parcel.

DISCUSSION

Under the Palmdale DC Industrial project (currently under construction), the intersection
of 10th Street West and Columbia Way (Avenue M) will be built out and constructed to
ultimate conditions. As described in Exhibits ‘A’ and ‘B’, these roadway improvements
will provide roadway widening, drainage upgrades, bike lanes, traffic signal
modifications, and street lighting along 10th Street West and Columbia Way (Avenue M).
Resolution No. CC 2024-089 will authorize the public use of portions of APN 3128-015-
903 for road and highway purposes.

FISCAL IMPACT

$0; There is no fiscal impact to the City as the developer is completing all roadway and
bikeway improvements along 10th Street West and Columbia Way (Avenue M).

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-090, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
  Palmdale authorizing the execution of a grand deed for portions of City-owned land
  to the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) for Parcel 79478-1,
  identified in Right of Way Appraisal Map Nos. 27055-C and 27056-C;

  2. Authorize the Mayor to execute Resolution No. CC 2024-090, a Resolution of the
  City Council of the City of Palmdale authorizing the execution of a grant deed for
  portions of City-owned land to Caltrans for Parcel 79478-1, identified in Right of
  Way Appraisal Map Nos. 27055-C and 27056-C; and,

  3. Authorize the Mayor to execute a grant deed for portions of City-owned land to
  Caltrans for Parcel 79478-1, identified in Right of Way Appraisal Map Nos.
  27055-C and 27056-C.

BACKGROUND

On October 17, 2007, the City received a 1.47-acre parcel of land along State Route
138/47th Street East from Hoprock Palmdale, LLC, a Delaware company. This property
was given to the City as part of the developer’s obligation to provide land for road use,
as required by the approval conditions of Tentative Parcel Map No. 66322 and
Conditional Use Permit No. 06-03. This parcel's improvements include pavement
 Report to Mayor and City Council

widening, curb and gutter, sidewalk, drainage, traffic signal modifications, and street
lighting. The City was responsible for purchasing the required land before construction
and transferring ownership to Caltrans after the improvements were accepted. Caltrans
has notified the City to relinquish this parcel for highway use.

DISCUSSION

Caltrans has conducted a right-of-way appraisal of said property under Appraisal Map
Nos. 27055-C and 27056-C and has sent the City Certificate of Sufficiency for Parcel
79478-1. As part of the appraisal process, Caltrans has completed its environmental
review and submitted the Hazardous Materials Disclosure Document. The legal
description of Parcel 79478-1 is consistent with the grant deed accepted by the City.
Resolution No. CC 2024-090 will approve the transfer of ownership of Parcel 79478-1 to
Caltrans.

FISCAL IMPACT

$0; The City will not experience a fiscal impact, as maintenance responsibilities along the
portion of Highway 138/47th Street East will transfer to Caltrans.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the First Amendment to Memorandum of Understanding No. A-8029 with
  the Housing Authority of the City of Palmdale (Housing Authority) to provide an
  increase of $600,000 of the United States Treasury Coronavirus SLFRF under the
  ARPA funds for the development of affordable housing; and,

  2. Authorize the Executive Director or her designee to execute the First Amendment
  to Memorandum of Understanding Agreement No. A-8029 with the Housing
  Authority of the City of Palmdale, including minimal and/or non-substantial
  changes.

BACKGROUND

The City was awarded $35,445,019 from the U.S. Treasury through the Coronavirus
SLFRF under the ARPA. These funds can be used for various purposes, including
investing in affordable housing to help low-income residents and address the financial
challenges caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. The final rules allow the City to use
these funds to tackle the ongoing housing shortages worsened by the pandemic. Any
program income from repaid loans can be reused for eligible purposes, but there are
restrictions on when the funds can be used.

DISCUSSION

The Housing Authority assists developers with gap financing to develop and rehabilitate
affordable units for eligible households with extremely low, very low, and low incomes.
The Housing Authority proposes to loan the ARPA funds granted by the City and program
income received through repayment of the funds from a prior project to develop an eligible
affordable housing project. The Housing Authority plans to use ARPA funds to enter into
a proposed pre-development loan agreement with Linc 4th Street Palmdale, LP. This
agreement will help assess the feasibility of the proposed project, design it, and apply for
the necessary government approvals and financing.

FISCAL IMPACT

$600,000; ARPA funds are available.

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CHARTERED
  CITY OF PALMDALE, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING SECTION
  2.08.040 OF CHAPTER 2.08 OF TITLE 2 OF THE PALMDALE
  MUNICIPAL CODE, ESTABLISHING THE CITY COUNCIL’S
  REGULAR MEETING DAY, TIME AND PLACE.

 I.  Intent of the City Council

  a) The City Council is a strict supporter of the open meeting law known and referenced
  as the Brown Act. The Brown Act is a transparency driven law that requires all non-
  privileged city business to be conducted in public so that all can follow, participate in
  and communicate upon the business of the City.

  As business meetings under the Brown Act, it is clear that the intent and focus of public
  business meetings is to conduct the business affairs of the City rather than such
  meetings being town halls, study sessions or opinion gathering sessions. The Brown
  Act makes clear that nonbusiness items, regardless of the source, are not to be
  discussed, resolved or acted upon by the City Council as they are not accepted and
  agendized business matters. Speakers are provided public comment rights, but those
  are primarily directed to properly agendized, rather than ad hoc topics or issues.

  b) The business, adjudicative and legislative items the City Council addresses generally
  are in relation to business which the City is contracting with, regulating or taking
  legislative actions that apply to the business entity, industry or group that are most able
  to participate during normal 8 am – 5 pm, Monday through Friday, working hours.
  The interaction between the City Council and those directly involved in the business
  matters is best conducted during these regular business hours.

  c) All legal conditions precedent to the adoption of this Ordinance have occurred as
  required by law.

II.  Ordinance

  Now, Therefore:

  The City Council of the City of Palmdale does ordain as follows:

  1. In all respects as set forth in Part I, Intent of the City Council, which section is hereby
  incorporated by reference herein.

  2. Section “2.08.040 – Regular meeting day, time and place” shall be revoked and
  removed in its entirety and replaced with a new Section 2.08.040 of Chapter 2.08 of
  Title 2 of the Palmdale Municipal Code, to read, in words and figures, as follows:

  “2.08.040 Regular meeting day, time, and place.

  Phase 1 Public Facilities) 2025 Special Tax Bonds.

BACKGROUND

In September 2022, RdR Development Holdings, LLC (RdR), the property owner and
master developer of the Ritter Ranch property (Project), requested that the City form a
new community facilities district for the Phase 1 property portion of the Project to fund
public infrastructure and improvements necessary for the development of that first phase
(Phase 1). Phase 1 is expected to include up to 1,180 residential units. The City formed
the City of Palmdale Community Facilities District No. 2022-3 (Ritter Ranch Phase 1
Public Facilities) (CFD 2022-3) in late 2022. At the same time, the City formed the City
of Palmdale Community Facilities District No. 2022-2 (CFD 2022-2) to pay for City
services required as a result of the development of Phase 1.

Since the formation of CFD 2022-3, RdR has been involved in discussions with
homebuilders and has developed different strategies over time with respect to the tax
rates to be levied in Phase 1. RdR has requested that the City proceed with altering the
current Amended and Restated Rate and Method of Apportionment of Special Taxes
prior to the approval of the first series of Special Tax Bonds for CFD 2022-3 (Bonds),
expected to be issued in the coming months.

DISCUSSION

During the CFD 2022-3 formation process, special tax rates were established pursuant
to a Rate and Method of Apportionment of Special Taxes (2022 RMA), which is the
document that governs how special taxes will be levied on property within CFD 2022-3.
The special tax rates for CFD 2022-3 to pay for Bonds issued to fund public facilities
were designed so that the total property tax burden on each dwelling unit will not exceed
2% of the projected/assumed assessed value of such property. This tax burden
 Report to Mayor and City Council

incorporates all ad valorem taxes – the 1% general levy and any school, college, or
AVEK general obligation bond tax levy – as well as any special assessments or fees
included on the property tax bill. These additional special assessments also include the
special taxes for the City’s Services CFD 2022-2, which is contiguous with the property
in CFD 2022-3.

By early 2024, RdR had filed Tentative Tract Maps and had a clear idea of the lot sizes
in Phase 1. Further, home prices had declined and, to calculate any adjustments to the
maximum CFD 2022-3 special tax rates, the City commissioned a new Price Point Study
(2023 PPS) to determine a reasonable sales price for each unit type proposed for Phase
1. As a result of the prices shown in the 2023 PPS, as well as adjustments needed
resulting from better lot size information, special tax rates were reduced, and lot size
adjustments were made to the 2022 RMA. In addition, RdR requested an additional
special tax reduction to be applied to the first three tracts they expected to sell to
merchant builders. The City’s Special Tax Consultant prepared an Amended and
Restated Rate and Method of Apportionment of Special Tax (“Amended RMA”) to take
these various factors into account and include the special tax rate adjustments. The
Amended RMA was approved in March 2024.

Since March 2024, RdR has continued their discussions with merchant builders.
Although the overall concept is the same – provide lower taxes for the initial tracts to be
sold to homebuilders, the specific tracts that RdR may want to market first may change.
To that end, it is beneficial to remove the three specific tracts designated with lower tax
rates from the Amended RMA and provide for a tract-by-tract reduction in tax rates
administratively when the marketing plan is more clearly defined in early 2025.
Achieving this flexibility requires the approval of a Second Amended and Restated Rate
and Method of Apportionment of Special Tax (Second Amended and Restated RMA).

The City Council adopted a resolution of consideration to alter the Amended RMA for
CFD 2022-3 on November 6, 2024, and set December 18, 2024, as the date to hold the
required public hearing and complete the alteration process.

Alteration of RMA
The staff recommends that the City Council hold a public hearing to accept public
testimony on the proposed alteration of the RMA. After conducting the public hearing,
staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-092, which:
    alters the RMA, and,
    submits the alteration of the RMA to the qualified elector of the territory within
  CFD 2022-3.
After the Resolution is adopted, the City Clerk will conduct the special election and open
the ballot submitted by RdR, the qualified landowner elector.

    directs recording of a second amendment to the Amended and Restated Notice

After the adoption of this resolution, the alteration proceedings will be complete.
Supplement to Acquisition Agreement
The City Council approved the issuance of the first series of Bonds on November 20,
2024. The infrastructure expected to be funded with this current series of Bonds includes
street improvements, domestic water facilities, and sewer and storm drain facilities. The
entire list of facilities authorized to be funded by the Bonds is listed in the Acquisition
Agreement Supplement and is also being considered at this meeting. The City and RdR
are parties to an Acquisition Agreement, dated as of November 1, 2022, relating to the
construction by RdR of some of the infrastructure for CFD 2022-3. The parties are
required to approve a Supplement No. 1 to Acquisition Agreement (Acquisition
Agreement Supplement) to update the type of facilities to be financed and the budget for
the infrastructure to be constructed by the RdR.

  RESOLUTION NO. CC 2024-092

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE
  CALLING SPECIAL ELECTION REGARDING ALTERATION OF THE
  AMENDED RATE AND METHOD OF APPORTIONMENT OF SPECIAL
  TAXES FOR THE CITY OF PALMDALE COMMUNITY FACILITIES
  DISTRICT NO. 2022-3 (RITTER RANCH PHASE 1 PUBLIC FACILITIES)

  WHEREAS, on November 6, 2024, this City Council adopted Resolution No. CC
2024-081 entitled “A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Palmdale of
Consideration to Alter the Rate and Method of Apportionment of Special Taxes for the
City of Palmdale Community Facilities District No. 2022-3 (Ritter Ranch Phase 1 Public
Facilities)” (the “Resolution of Consideration”), proposing to alter the rate and method of
apportionment of the special taxes, as amended (the “Rate and Method”) for the City of
Palmdale Community Facilities District No. 2022-3 (Ritter Ranch Phase 1 Public
Facilities) (the “District”), all pursuant to the Mello-Roos Community Facilities Act of
1982, as amended, constituting Chapter 2.5 of Part 1 of Division 2 of Title 5,
commencing with Section 53311, of the California Government Code (the “Act”); and

  WHEREAS, the Resolution of Consideration, which makes reference to the map
of the boundaries of the District, and which contains a proposed second amended and
restated rate and method of apportionment for the District (the “Second Amended Rate
and Method”), is on file with the City Clerk and the provisions thereof are incorporated
herein by this reference as if fully set forth herein; and

  WHEREAS, the owner of all of the property in the District, RdR Development
Holdings, LLC, has requested that the City Council take the actions necessary to alter
the Amended Rate and Method; and

  WHEREAS, on the date hereof, the City Council held a noticed public hearing as
required by the Act and the Resolution of Consideration relative to the proposed
changes to the Second Amended Rate and Method; and

  WHEREAS, at said hearing all property owners and any other interested persons
with respect to the District desiring to be heard on all matters pertaining to the proposed
changes to the Second Amended Rate and Method were heard and a full and fair
hearing was held; and

  WHEREAS, written protests with respect to the proposed changes to the Second
Amended Rate and Method have not been filed with the City Clerk by fifty percent (50%)
or more of any registered voters residing within the territory of the District or property
 Resolution No. CC 2024-092
Page 2 of 5
owners of one-half (1/2) or more of the area of land within the District and not exempt
from the levy of the special tax; and

  WHEREAS, the proposition of the approval of the changes to the Second
Amended Rate and Method shall be submitted to the qualified elector of the District as
required by the Act.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The foregoing recitals are true and correct.

  SECTION 2. The proposed changes to the Rate and Method of the special tax to
be levied within the District by the Second Amended Rate and Method has not been
precluded by majority protest pursuant to Section 53337 of the Act.

  SECTION 3. All prior proceedings taken by the City Council in connection with the
proposed alteration of the Second Amended Rate and Method for the District, as set
forth in the Resolution of Consideration, have been duly considered and are hereby
found and determined to be valid and in conformity with the requirements of the Act

  SECTION 4. Subject to the approval of the qualified elector of the District at the
special election referred to below, the Rate and Method is hereby altered by the Second
Amended and Restated Rate and Method of Apportionment of Special Taxes specified
in the Resolution No. CC 2024-081 of the City Council adopted November 6, 2024, and
shall be the Second Amended Rate and Method set forth in Exhibit A attached to the
Resolution of Consideration.

  SECTION 5. Pursuant to Sections 53338(a) and 53326 of the Act, the issue of the
approval of the Second Amended Rate and Method shall be submitted to the qualified
elector of the District at an election called therefor as provided below.

  SECTION 6. The ballot measure shall be in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A
and by this reference incorporated herein, and said form of ballot is hereby approved.

  SECTION 7. The City Council hereby finds that fewer than 12 persons have been
registered to vote within the territory of the District for each of the ninety (90) days
preceding the close of the public hearing heretofore conducted and concluded by the
City Council for the purposes of these proceedings. Accordingly, and pursuant to
Section 53326 of the Act, the City Council finds that for purposes of these proceedings,
the sole qualified elector for the District is the sole owner of the land within the District
and that the vote shall be by said landowner, having one vote for each acre or portion
of an acre such landowner owns in the District as of the close of the public hearing.

  SECTION 8. The City Council hereby calls a special election to consider the
measure described in Section 6 above, which election shall be held immediately
 Resolution No. CC 2024-092
Page 3 of 5
following adoption of this Resolution in the City Council Chambers. The Acting City Clerk
is hereby designated as the official to conduct said election. It is hereby acknowledged
that the City Clerk has on file a copy of this Resolution, a map of the boundaries of the
District,

  SECTION 9. The voted ballot shall be returned to the City Clerk immediately
following adoption of this Resolution, and when the sole qualified elector has voted, the
election shall be closed.

  SECTION 10. Pursuant to Sections 53326(b) and 53327 of the Act, the election
shall be conducted by mail ballot pursuant to applicable provisions of the Act and of the
California Elections Code.

  SECTION 11. The City Council acknowledges that the City Clerk has caused to
be delivered to the sole qualified elector of the District a ballot in the form set forth in
Exhibit “A” hereto.

  The ballot was accompanied by all supplies and written instructions necessary to
the use and return of the ballot. The envelope to be used to return the ballot was
enclosed with the ballot, had the return postage prepaid, and contained the following:
(a) the name and address of the landowner, (b) a declaration, under penalty of perjury,
stating that the voter is owner of record or authorized representative of the landowner
entitled to vote and is the person whose name appears on the envelope, (c) the printed
name, signature and address of the voter, (d) the date of signing and place of execution
of the declaration pursuant to clause (b) above, and (e) a notice that the envelope
contains an official ballot and is to be opened only by the canvassing board.

  Analysis and arguments with respect to the ballot measure have been waived by
the landowner voter, by means of the waiver contained in its voted ballot, all as permitted
by Section 53327(b) of the Act. The City Council hereby concurs in said waiver.

  SECTION 12. The City Clerk shall accept the ballot of the qualified elector in the
City Council Chambers upon and prior to the adoption of this Resolution, whether said
ballot be personally delivered or received by mail. The City Clerk shall have available a
ballot which may be marked at said location on the election day by said qualified elector.

  SECTION 13. The City Council hereby further finds that the provision of Section
53326 of the Act requiring a minimum of 90 days following the adoption of the resolution
of calling the election to elapse before the special election is for the protection of the
qualified elector of the District. The voted ballot of the sole qualified elector of the District
contains a waiver of the time for said special election. Accordingly, this City Council finds
and determines that if the qualified elector submits its voted ballot in the election, the
qualified elector will have agreed to the shortened time for the election and will thereby
have been fully protected in these proceedings. This City Council also finds and
determines that the City Clerk has concurred in the shortened time for the election.

November 1, 2022 (the “Original Agreement”) relating to the construction by the Master
Developer of some of the Facilities; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council now desires to approve Supplement No. 1 to
Acquisition Agreement No. A-8174 (“Supplement No. 1”) to update the listed Facilities
and Discrete Components in the Original Agreement, and to extend the effective date of
the Original Agreement.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

the form presented at this meeting, is hereby approved by the City Council. The Mayor,
the City Manager, and the Director of Operations (each, a “Designated Officer”), each
acting alone, are hereby authorized, for and in the name and on behalf of the City, to
execute and deliver Supplement No. 1 in said form together with such additions thereto

No. 1 upon consultation with the City Attorney and Bond Counsel, the approval of such

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Receive public testimony regarding proposed Ordinance No. 1647;

  2. Adopt Ordinance No. 1647 approving Zoning Ordinance Amendment (ZOA) 24-
  0001; and,

  3. Find that the request is consistent with Program Environmental Impact Report
  (PEIR) 22-002 prepared and certified in conjunction with the City’s General Plan
  (Palmdale 2045)

BACKGROUND

On September 21, 2022, Palmdale 2045 was adopted by the City Council and replaced
the previously adopted General Plan (1993). State law requires that the regulations
governing the use and development of lands within the municipal limits of a city be
consistent with the adopted General Plan for that city. ZOA 21-007 was adopted by the
City Council on March 15, 2023, which amended Title 17 of the Palmdale Municipal Code
(PMC) to implement the vision of Palmdale 2045 as well as support new land use patterns
and future development. Since then, staff identified minor amendments to Title 17, which
are necessary to address review procedures and streamline review processes for City
projects.

On November 21, 2024, the Planning Commission adopted Resolution No. PC-2024-023
recommending City Council approval of ZOA 24-0001.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Ord. No. 1647
December 18, 2024
Page 2

DISCUSSION

Section 500 of the Palmdale City Charter grants the City of Palmdale full authority to
regulate local land use and public facilities. As such, City staff is requesting a streamlined
approval process for City projects. The proposed ZOA would allow the City Manager or
her designee to approve these projects administratively at her discretion. Approval of the
proposed ZOA would expedite the review and approval process for City projects,
ultimately preserving staff resources, time, and reducing project costs.

Map update. Staff review has determined that a subsequent or supplemental PEIR as
described in California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Sections 15162,
15163, or 15164, is not required because the proposed ZOA would not require major

  REDUCED TRANSACTIONS AND USE TAX, AND ADOPT
  RESOLUTION NO. 2024-096, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY

  IMPLEMENTATION OF THE TRANSACTIONS AND USE TAX
  INCREASE AUTHORIZED BY AB 2443 AND ENACTED BY

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Introduce and Adopt Ordinance No. 1650, an Ordinance of the City Council of the
  City of Palmdale amending Section 3.21 of the Palmdale Municipal Code relating
  to the implementation and collection of reduced transactions and use tax; and,

  2. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-096, a Resolution of the City Council of the City
  of Palmdale phasing the implementation of the transactions and use tax increase
  authorized by AB 2443 and enacted by Measure PD.

BACKGROUND

On November 3, 2020, voters passed Measure AV, which enacted Chapter 3.21 of the
Palmdale Municipal Code and established an additional sales tax of 0.75% within the
City of Palmdale (“City”) to fund essential services including, but not limited to, street
repair, addressing homelessness, emergency response, public safety, maintaining local
businesses, protecting water resources, and programs for seniors, veterans, mental
health and the community.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Ord. No. 1650 and Reso. No. CC 2024-096
December 18, 2024
Page 2

On November 5, 2024, the City of Palmdale voters passed Measure PD, which amended
Chapter 3.21 of the Palmdale Municipal Code and established an automatic increase of
the City’s Transactions and Use Tax if, whenever, and to the extent permitted by
applicable law. Measure PD establishes the City’s Transactions and Use Tax as the
maximum rate permitted by law, but is silent as to how, when, and to what extent the
City must implement and collect the maximum rate, or whether, in the alternative, the
City may phase, defer, or otherwise implement and collect a lower rate.

DISCUSSION

This proposed ordinance adds a new Section 3.21.035 to the Palmdale Municipal Code
that authorizes the City Council, by resolution or other action, to phase, defer, or
otherwise implement and collect a rate that is lower than the full rate established by
Sections 3.21.040 and/or 3.21.060. Notwithstanding any such phasing, deferral, or other
reduced collection, the rates established by Sections 3.21.040 and 3.21.060 shall
remain the City’s authorized, approved, and established Transactions and Use Tax
rates. The City Council may exercise its authority, under this proposed ordinance only
as and to the extent permitted by law. Nothing in this proposed ordinance authorizes the
City Council to impose a tax rate increase that would exceed the maximum rates
established by Sections 3.21.040 and 3.21.060 or require voter approval.

The proposed resolution defers until January 1, 2028, the implementation and collection
of one-quarter (1/4); and defers until January 1, 2029, the implementation and collection
of the final one-quarter (1/4) of the 1% transactions and use tax increase authorized by
AB 2443 and enacted by Measure PD (i.e., 0.5%).

FISCAL IMPACT

The fiscal impact associated with this action is unknown at this time.

STRATEGIC PLAN

  transparency.
